title: Ivo and the Letter
premise: In the winter of 1899, Rafael Halloran serves as a battlefield nurse in a garrison town, secretly keeping a ledger of soldiers' names that official reports omit. When the army requisitions the town and confiscates all written records, Rafael's sister Ivo — who has lived disguised as a man to survive — becomes both the ledger's keeper and its most dangerous entry. As evacuation orders arrive, the family must decide who takes the single last berth on the departing ship before the century turns. In the end, Rafael gives the berth to Ivo, stays behind with the ledger hidden in a wounded soldier's coat, and discovers that survival means being remembered by someone else.
about_author: Noor Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed letters in municipal repositories across northern Europe. They write historical fiction about the people official records forget.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. In the garrison hospital, Rafael records names officers omit in a cloth-bound ledger, measuring each patient in what can be carried: a button, a photograph, a name. Emotional beat: quiet defiance established; the ledger introduced as an act of witness.

chapters.title: Ivo in the Ward
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Disguised as a male hospital orderly, Ivo tends the dying while guarding her secret, watching Rafael write names she knows are her own aliases among them. Emotional beat: tension between invisibility as safety and invisibility as erasure.

chapters.title: What the Officers Omit
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A colonel demands the ward's casualty list; Rafael hands over the official version and hides the true ledger beneath floorboards. A dying soldier entrusts Rafael with an unsent letter home. Emotional beat: first taste of real danger.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Soldiers chalk numbers on doors; the army requisitions the town, its stores, its paper. Ivo watches men inventory everything, including people. Emotional beat: the world shrinks to what can be carried.

chapters.title: The Confiscation Order
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. An order arrives: all written records, private and public, to be surrendered for inspection. Rafael must move the ledger or lose every name. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Hiding Places
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Sibling and sibling argue over where to hide the ledger — the well, the chapel wall, a dead man's coat. Ivo insists on sewing it into a soldier's greatcoat bound for the depot. Emotional beat: trust tested between brother and sister.

chapters.title: The Inspection
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Officers comb the hospital; a young lieutenant lingers over Rafael's neat hand and asks questions that feel like traps. The ledger survives by hours. Emotional beat: paranoia; the sense of being seen at last.

chapters.title: Berths
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Evacuation is announced: one ship before the century turns, limited berths, families split by lottery and rank. Ivo learns her papers could unravel at any checkpoint. Emotional beat: hope curdling into arithmetic — who gets to leave?

chapters.title: Mother's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The siblings' mother forces the question into the open: someone stays. Old grievances surface about who was allowed to disappear into disguise and who kept the household standing. Emotional beat: family fracture along the fault line of sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Lieutenant's Letter
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The young lieutenant from the inspection returns, wounded, and Ivo nurses him; he carries confiscated letters he was ordered to burn and hasn't. Emotional beat: unexpected kinship; the enemy revealed as another keeper of names.

chapters.title: A Coat Full of Witnesses
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The greatcoat holding the ledger is loaded onto a supply cart headed the wrong way. Rafael trades a week of morphine rations to track it through the occupied quarter. Emotional beat: desperation; the cost of memory made literal.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at the Mill Bridge
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Escorting the coat, Ivo is stopped; a clerk reads her papers aloud and hesitates over one letter of one name. She talks her way through by reciting the dead — the ledger's litany — from memory. Emotional beat: identity as performance, perilously close to exposure.

chapters.title: What Rafael Carries
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Flashback chapter: how Rafael began the ledger after abandoning a patient whose name no report recorded. Emotional beat: grief explained; the theme of the price of survival given its roots.

chapters.title: The Lottery
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Berth assignments posted. By clerical accident, two names appear where only one berth exists: Rafael's and Ivo's. The family has three days to resolve it before the error is corrected for them. Emotional beat: fate forcing the choice they dreaded.

chapters.title: Arguments at the Waterline
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. On the frozen quay, the family argues through the night. Mother declares she will stay; Rafael refuses to let her; Ivo quietly arranges to give up her own place. Emotional beat: love expressed as stubbornness.

chapters.title: The Lieutenant's Choice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The lieutenant, able to alter the manifest, offers to strike any name — if Rafael surrenders the ledger openly. He wants to save one person honestly rather than everyone corruptly. Emotional beat: moral climax approaching; integrity versus lives.

chapters.title: Century's Eve
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. New Year's Eve. Bells, bonfires, embarkation at midnight. Rafael copies the ledger's names into memory and small tokens, preparing to surrender the book. Emotional beat: solemnity; the century ending as a door closing.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the gangway, Rafael puts Ivo aboard and steps back, pressing the dead soldier's unsent letter into her hands. Ivo fights to stay; the ship's bell ends the argument. Emotional beat: heartbreak; the choice made and irreversible.

chapters.title: Surrender of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael hands the ledger to the lieutenant on the empty quay, asking only that the names be read aloud once, somewhere, someday. The lieutenant salutes instead of arresting. Emotional beat: catharsis; witness transferred, not destroyed.

chapters.title: Staying Invisible Was Never an Option
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael remains in the requisitioned town as a nurse to those too broken to ship out, no longer hiding, tending under their own true name. Emotional beat: transformation; survival redefined as presence rather than disappearance.

chapters.title: Letters Across the Water
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, years later. From a new country, Ivo writes letters to every family on the ledger's list, returning names to the living. One reply comes from the lieutenant, now old, enclosing pages he copied before burning the rest. Emotional beat: bittersweet restoration; memory outlives paper.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, final chapter. In a village hall, the recovered names are read aloud while Rafael, gray now, listens from the back row; Ivo stands beside them. The last name read is their mother's. Emotional beat: resolution and grace — what can be carried, finally, is each other.
